summary: Restore the prefix in the sense vorenthalten
rationale: The associated example lo=kə-mḥame tu mede meni is translated er enthält mir nichts vor. The infinitive for that separable verb is vorenthalten; the gloss has lost vor-.

summary: Correct 'stürzt' to 'schützt'

summary: II mḥame and III maḥme are separately supported by the vowel order; the Arabic source stem number does not determine the Turoyo stem.
II protection permits a zero-marked protected object with m- threat and a possible ʕal- threat. III corpus examples consistently use active reflexive ruḥo, not Detransitive morphology.
The III Infectum material was not absent from the entry: Bsorino/1 was embedded in the sense text. The new box organizes existing evidence, while 113/24 adds Infectum-wa.
MAC NE Interview 2/223 contrasts -nxu with -lxu patient suffixes. These variants remain source forms; no separate lexical sense follows.
All 14 occurrences reviewed. Jan adds two protection Preterit contexts and the decisive II reflexive example; most Infectum tokens are redundant after round 1.
mḥamele aʕlayye is read as protection from the parallel not-standing-up-for-the-Christians discourse; the homographic ḥml reading is not selected mechanically.
Protection has zero-marked themes, suffixed themes and aʕlayye. The explicit lam məḏyoye agent at 3.15/184 helps distinguish the Preterit frame.
Lookup of ḥym and ḥmm confirmed heat/fever and bathing families, but did not establish the derivation of the charcoal warming form. No unrelated entry is altered.
72/4: confirm attachment of ʕal ad debure to mḥamən across the yatiwo relative rather than to sitting.

Do II and III distinguish protection of another from self-defence systematically, or is the present corpus distribution accidental? Three III contexts have ruḥo but are insufficient for a categorical rule.
At Jan 1.16/737 is mḥamanwo ruḥayye mu quro lexical warming or protecting oneself from cold? Elicit the base form before adding II Infectum-wa.
At 3.13/125 confirm whether mḥamanne is Preterit or an unprefixed Infectum in past discourse.
Confirm ʕal patient government in 1.41/1824; Jan English is machine translation.

rationale: Other stands for the other four people here and needs the plural nominal form others; no following noun licenses the adjective other.
